To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the major BLV core protein (p 24) contains two T cell epitopes, which are recognized by CD4 T cells from BLV-infected animals with a normal lymphocyte count.
the p24 protein of bovine leukaemogenic virus (BLV) contains two regions which are recognized by T cells from BLV-infected animals.
the p24 protein of BLV contains at least two immunodominant regions recognized by CD4 T cells of BLV-infected cows with normal haematologic values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a T cell-based diagnostic assay for BLV infection in cattle.
the characterization of T cell epitope(s) recognized by CD4 T lymphocytes in BLV-inflicted cattle.
the identification of T cell determinants on the p24 protein of BLV and with the characterization of the immune response to this antigen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cell proliferative response in BLV-infector cattle with normal haemotological values is not related to the presence of lymphocytosis.
BLV infection is not associated with the development of a specific cell-mediated immunity in the host, at least in the animals tested.
the proliferative response observed is a T cell-mediated immune response to the p24 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p24 protein is a major antigen in the BLV-infected animals and that the immune response to this protein may be important to the development of persistent lymphocytoses.
we identified a T cell epitope of p24 in BLV-infaced cattle, and this epitope may have a role in the pathogenesis of BLV.
BLV infection is associated with a specific T cell response to the p24 protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response against BLV p24 protein is complex and that it involves several epitopes, which are located in different regions of the protein.
the T cell proliferative response against the BLV p24 protein is restricted to animals with normal haematopoietic values.
the T cell proliferative response of BLV-infected cows with normal blood counts can be used as a marker for BLV infection.
